notes.6i: There were a fair number of candidates who did not respond to this question at all but there were many who recognised that what was required was the number of permutations of 4 items from 5 and got the answer easily.
notes.6iii: Many realised that the number of ways for first and last was 4P and the number of ways for the middle three was 7P . The only issue was those who thought that one was a prime number. Answers: (i) 120 (ii) 720 (iii) 2520
notes.7i: The responses to this question fell into three categories in the main. Firstly there were those who were familiar with the requirement, could add fractions, knew their trig identities and scored full marks. Secondly there were those who struggled with the algebra and knew little trig, even ending up inventing identities and scored at most one mark. Finally there were those who realised their limitations and moved on to the next question.
notes.7iii: Candidates used the given expression in order to obtain an equation in tan2x , sin2x or cos2x and a number then solved to find values of x. Unfortunately, many took only the positive square root and so obtained just two values rather than four. Answers: (ii) 0.955, 2.19, 4.10, 5.33 �PAGE�17
notes.8i: This question was done well only by the better candidates. Of the others there were those who knew that they had to use calculus but did not differentiate well and then there were others who attempted to find the equation by other means. There were a number who did not attempt this part at all.
notes.8iii: This part also proved demanding for many of the candidates and a number, once again, made no attempt. Those who did attempt it knew to find the area of the trapezium and then integrate the curve between the given limits. Many did not get the integral correct but did obtain some credit for their other work. Answers: (i) y = x+1 (ii) 15.5

notes.key_messages:
Candidates should be encouraged to attempt all questions. Often, the first mark or two can be earned by
making a start at a question even if the candidate is unable to complete it.
Candidates need to take care with their algebra to ensure that marks are not lost through careless slips.
notes.general_comments:
The quality of presentation has improved this year. There has been less irrelevant working which can lead to
confusion to both the candidate themself and the Examiner. Many candidates could show that they had a
good grasp of all areas of the syllabus. However, many candidates appeared to have less than a full
understanding of all the topic areas. It is important that candidates have covered the whole syllabus.
